llm.summary: This is a coherent Cargo analytics skill, but it can export workspace data and includes an explicit rerun command that users should run carefully.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is monitoring run metrics, downloading run results, and exporting segment data, which matches most documented commands. The failed-record rerun example is operational rather than passive analytics, but it is presented as a manual recovery step after fixing an issue.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill gives concrete CLI examples and identifies read-only SQL only for the query command; it does not hide broader download or export behavior. It would benefit from stronger warnings before state-changing reruns and bulk exports.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact is markdown documentation and declares installation of the external @cargo-ai/cli npm package; no embedded scripts, obfuscation, or automatic execution were found in the skill files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Cargo account access and workspace-scoped credentials are expected for this integration. Export and download commands may retrieve sensitive workflow, customer, or business data, so scope filters and local handling matter.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No background persistence, privilege escalation, local indexing, or hidden credential collection is present. Actions occur only through user-invoked Cargo CLI commands.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust Cargo and are authorized to access the workspace data. Prefer OAuth over pasted tokens, avoid sharing signed download URLs or exported files, use the narrowest filters and limits possible, and confirm explicitly before running the failed-record rerun command because it can trigger workflow activity and consume credits.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: The batch-create example is a real state-changing recovery action, not a passive metric query. It is visible and related to failed-run handling, so it is guidance-worthy rather than evidence of deception.
[SDI-4] expected: The read-only statement applies to the SQL query command specifically. The wider skill also documents downloads and one rerun action, so users should not treat the whole skill as read-only.
[SQP-2] expected: Run downloads, node-output URLs, and segment exports are central to the skill's purpose, but the documentation should make clear that exported data and signed URLs can be sensitive.
[SQP-2] expected: API-token authentication is expected for non-interactive CLI use, and OAuth is recommended. Tokens should still be treated as workspace secrets and kept out of logs and transcripts.
[SQP-2] expected: The export examples legitimately support analytics use cases, including filtered customer or account fields, but users should limit scope and store exported files only in approved environments.
